newsitem.title: UK: Young viewers disappointed by UK's C5 TV - survey.
newsitem.headline: Young viewers disappointed by UK's C5 TV - survey.

text.p: More than a third of 15-24 year-olds say that new UK television station Channel 5 is not as good as expected and worse than rival channels, media research specialist CIA MediaLab said on Monday.
Channel 5, launched on March 30, has aimed particularly at the under-35 audience.

CIA, which carries out a monthly survey of 500 adults, said that 35 percent of 15-24 year-olds questioned said the channel had failed to come up to expectations and 38 percent said it was worse than rival channels.

Across the population as a whole, 21 percent think that Channel 5 is worse than other channels and 13 percent say it is below expectations. Only seven percent say it is better than expected and a mere two percent say it is better than its rivals.
Reception is a problem, with more than half of those questioned saying that they either cannot pick up the channel or have poor reception.
"Channel 5 has the potential to attract a larger audience," said Anthony Jones, head of CIA MediaLab.
"As reception, rather than programming, seems to be one of the main reasons why a lot of people do not currently watch, C5 must continue to find new and improved ways of delivering its signal."
Channel 5, in which Pearson Plc and United News & Media Plc are key shareholders, has recently boosted its coverage by securing satellite distribution.
